rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty builder trees go (a row of magnolias, eucalyptus, jacarandas and ficus along the back fences, a queen palm and two norfolk pines 3 m from the house fronts, a few in the yards); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the adirondack chair, three swing sets, and the open south lot corners.

trees.why: the west back yard with the adirondack chair (1.2 m off): a jacaranda to sit under
the back yard with the swing set (2.6 m off): shade over the swings
the east back yard's swing set (2.6 m off): a magnolia over the swings
the south-west yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): shade over the swings
the south back lot line, 10 m from the houses: an old ficus between two yards
the open lot corner at the south-east, 20 m from the walls: a full jacaranda
